newsitem.title: INDONESIA: FOCUS-Jakarta stocks in record one-day plunge.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Jakarta stocks in record one-day plunge.

text.p: Investors went on a panic selling spree on the Jakarta stock market Friday, triggering the steepest-ever one-day plunge in the index and pushing it to its lowest level of the year.
Unnerved by the fall of the rupiah to another new low and the prospects of further currency weakness, investors sold stocks across the board, brokers said.

The composite index fell 25.31 points, or 3.94 percent, to 617.71 points. The only comparable decline in memory was the 3.66 percent slump on July 29 last year which followed the worst riots in Jakarta in two decades.

"Players are rushing to get out of the market as soon as possible and sell at whatever price they can due to the rupiah's plunge," said Yannes Naibaho, president and chief executive officer of UBS Sekuritas.
"It's a blue day today. We expect the weak market to remain for around three months," said Tom Inglis, head of research with ING Barings Indonesia.
Heavy selling by local and foreign players pushed about 20 percent of the approximately 250 listed firms to their lowest levels of the year, brokers said.
Blue chips Bank International Indonesia (BII), Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI), pulp and paper firm Indah Kiat and telecommunications giant Telkom were among the hardest hit.
Inglis said uncertainties in the market were likely to remain due to the rupiah and that market psychology was likely to rule over fundamentals.

"The stock market has become the victim of the currency markets. How long would the market remain like this? It will largely depend on the currency markets," Goei Siauw Hong, an analyst with Socgen Crosby Securities, said.

The rupiah fell to a new record low of 2,960 to the dollar in the afternoon from its opening level of 2,770/90, triggering strong selling in the stock market, brokers said. Reports that many Indonesian corporates had large unhedged exposures to foreign currency loans did not help, they added.
Among individual stocks, BII topped the active list, with 51 million shares traded. It fell 200 rupiah to close at a year-low of 1,200 rupiah.

Analysts said BII's falls were due to worries that the bank, which derives large parts of its net income from the foreign exchange market and trade financing, would be hit by the volatile currency markets.

BNI, the largest bank in the country, closed 150 rupiah lower at 1,200 rupiah after touching a year-low of 1,175 rupiah as the bank also sources most of its earnings from the foreign exchange market, analysts said.
But some analysts said the current weakness on the stock market could provide the springboard for a rebound.

"There are expectations that investors will come back (into the market) sooner than any other country in the region and I am very confident that the market turnaround will be quite strong," said Gunawan Jusuf, managing director of local brokerage Makindo Securities.

"The analysis so far has been that because of the government's prudent and consistent policies, macro-economic stability is quite solid," he told Reuters at the sidelines of an international capital market conference in Jakarta.

"In general, people will go back to fundamental evaluation, with macro-economic policy taking top place," he said, adding that investors would be coming back to the Indonesian stock market with an eye on strategic and undervalued sectors.
